says: fabsh's recall finds the current line with history.lastIndexOf(text), so once history holds a line twice, Up flips between the two newest lines and never reaches older ones, as bash's Up does.
proof: A scratch script ran read.ts's recall six times 'back' over history ["x","a","b","a"] from an empty line and printed ["a","b","a","b","a","b"]: "x" is never reached. No law covers recall walking the whole history; L4 only checks that the tile and the process agree.
cost: A person who repeats a command, the usual case in a shell, cannot get to anything older with Up.
